prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1113; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant, who is handling the matter without a lawyer. The claimant describes a side impact at an intersection and reports a back strain.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene, the other driver's statement, and the responding officer's notes all describe the collision the same way the claimant does. Witnesses at the scene also confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Inspection of the vehicle shows side damage consistent with the reported impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known to the adjuster at this point.

Entry 4: The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the first call and the follow-up interview. The reported back injury fits the kind and force of this crash.

Entry 5: A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with damage several weeks before the claimed accident date. This conflicts with the other information gathered and needs follow-up with the neighbor and the repair records.

Entry 6: The claimant's medical records show a treatment course typical for this type of strain, with visits tapering as the claimant improved. The records also note a minor strain in the same area years ago that healed completely.

Entry 7: The driver lives with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy. Coverage review is complete, and the file is ready for the next step in the claim process.
